pr_title: Remove thread contention from Activity Start/Stop
pr_body:
Fixes #107158 

This change tries to resolve a performance issue related to thread contention when starting and stopping Activities. The new approach is a lock-free, copy-on-write array design which eliminates all thread contention and improves the throughput of Activity.Start/Stop (based on local testing). 

I would like to add some basic tests to the `SynchronizedList<T>` class, but I'm unsure what the policy/procedure is for testing internal classes

I would also like to make sure that this PR has the desired effect of improving request throughput in key benchmarks when telemetry is enabled.


# The problem
The existing code was causing lock contention between request threads that were starting and stopping activities. The approach was to lock and unlock for each item in the collection. So if there were 10 listeners, the request thread would have to acquire and release 10 locks, each of which could contend with other request threads.

# Proposed solution
Use "immutable" arrays of listeners that can be acquired by a request thread without locking. This should make the common/hot path (starting/stopping activities) faster when the system is under load. It should, however, also have a small negative impact on adding/removing listeners, which now becomes a O(N) operation instead of the O(~1) that it was before. However in practice this should have essentially no impact on application performance or allocations

# Local Testing 

My methodology was to start multiple threads (16 vCore machine) and to Start/Stop Activities in a hot loop (worst case).

- 10 worker/request threads
- 50,000 start/dispose activities per thread
- 10 ActivityListeners subscribed up front and not mutated
- 10 runs of benchmark 

## Results Before Changes
Benchmark execution time `00:00:15.1899827`

![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/75a6ec53-f96e-48d2-934e-1901103acc5e)



## Results After Changes
Benchmark execution time `00:00:01.5148120`

![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/cd18bb45-2728-4ebf-9e2e-1c92c4423e74)

## Microbenchmarks
 - With Prometheus metrics exporter 
 - + AddRuntimeInstrumentation
 - 1 synthetic/null tracing/actvity processor
 - 1 synthetic activity listener (to verify invocation counts)
 - 50,000 activity start/stops per thread

issue_context.title: Adding OpenTelemetry instrumentation results in 15% RPS degradation
issue_context.body:
### Description

In the ASP.NET benchmarks, one of the scenarios we run is a "TODOs API" service which is basically a CRUD web api over top of a postgres database. We added it as part of our "cloud native" push in .NET 8. The intention was to track the perf difference between normal .NET, native AOT, trimming, etc.
 
It was always our intention to include OpenTelemetry in this scenario. It wasn't originally added because OpenTelemetry wasn't native AOT compatible at the time. But now it is, and I decided to enable the same configuration that [.NET Aspire defaults](https://github.com/dotnet/aspire/blob/main/src/Aspire.ProjectTemplates/templates/aspire-servicedefaults/Extensions.cs#L44-L89) to - [Add OpenTelemetry to TodosApi (aspnet/Benchmarks#2014)](https://github.com/aspnet/Benchmarks/pull/2014).
 
It adds tracing and metrics instrumentation, and the OTLP exporter configured on an environment variable. The environment variable isn't set in our system, so the telemetry doesn't go anywhere.

I would have thought there wouldn't be much runtime overhead in this scenario, but we are seeing a decent sized regression in RPS now that this is enabled.

### Configuration

.NET 9 recent daily builds. Windows and Linux x64.

### Regression?

This isn't a regression in .NET. But adding OpenTelemetry instrumentation to an application (even when there are no exporters) is a performance regression.

### Data

https://aka.ms/aspnet/nativeaot/benchmarks/

* On the "Native AOT" page - 18 of 21 - (which tracks the same benchmark apps against regular coreclr and native AOT. Note that this issue repros on both, so it isn't a native AOT issue).
* Select "Stage2" on the right. You can pick Intel Linux or Intel Windows at the top, or both.
* Notice the drop in RPS and the increase in average latency on Aug 20, 2024

![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/9c72c45f-f751-4262-9fe3-5688bf65c74b)

The RPS went from 270k => 230k on linux. This date is the first time the benchmark was run after https://github.com/aspnet/Benchmarks/pull/2014 was merged.

The following .zip contains before and after .nettrace files of the benchmark.
[OpenTelemetryTraces.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/16805325/OpenTelemetryTraces.zip)


### Analysis

Doing a diff between the 2, I see a bunch more "DotNETRuntime/Contention/Start" events in the "after" for System.Diagnostics.DiagnosticSource
 
#### Before:
![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/0d6a84c4-80f6-487a-822a-daab99426e77)

#### After:
![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/7452e627-0dd0-428a-8345-5680d4c210b5)

This appears to be the same issue as illustrated in this simplified repro: https://github.com/cijothomas/lock-contention-activity-repro/blob/main/lock-contention-activity-repro/Program.cs.

cc @noahfalk @tarekgh @cijothomas

> Sounds like the same problem as [dotnet/aspnetcore#50412](https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/issues/50412)

Not fully. Based on the traces shown in screenshot, contention is at the Activity level. There is some contention shown for Metric path too. I am yet to check the traces fully to see if it is at the MeterListener level, or occurring at OpenTelemetry level. (I doubt if it is at OTel level, as there is no "lock" statement used by OTel Metrics in hot path.)

Activity and Meter have the same mechanism in calling back the registered listener which requires the lock to avoid mutating the listeners list during the operation. We need to change that for both cases to avoid locking during the notification.

Interesting seeing this issue here, as we recently had to rollback our OpenTelemetry instrumentation in one of our tool applications.

We have a console app that executes tasks for our background task queue mechanism. In our beta environment, we have nearly 1000 instances of this same `.exe` process running, across just 2 servers. Those 2 servers usually run at 25 to 30% CPU usage. When a _very basic_ otel setup was introduced, usage capped the server at 100% CPU and would never drop from there: the environment stalled and we had to remove the instrumentation.

Because of this extreme performance effect, we currently have a custom feature toggle on our side that we check during initialization to conditionally call `AddOpenTelemetry` (and the rest of the OTEL setup) on a particular instance. So now we have OTEL enabled on just 3 or 4 out of the 1000 work types that we have (basically, one work type is mapped to one `.exe` instance).

Since our application is still using .NET 472, we've not pursued this much further for now as the intent was to reevaluate performance when we could perform the migration to .NET8, which is coming soon.

In our case, the degradation was _vastly_ more significant than 15%, and it seemed to impact the project _even if we removed every single instrumentation from the pipeline_, which was extremely surprising to me. It is as if just the presence of the built-in hosted services already adds the biggest chunk of the overhead, for whatever reason.

Another thing worth mentioning is that this tool does not have ASPNETCore involved at all. It is just a simple console application that runs on an infinite `while` loop, dequeueing and processing work based on an input parameter that indicates "which type of work it should dequeue/process".

> Activity and Meter have the same mechanism in calling back the registered listener which requires the lock to avoid mutating the listeners list during the operation. We need to change that for both cases to avoid locking during the notification.

I'm probably out of my depth here but a common pattern I use is to rely on `ImmutableArray` and `ImmutableInterlocked` so that readers don't need to obtain locks. This obviously comes at the expense of latency when the list needs to be mutated, but that operation is non-blocking also at least

> Another thing worth mentioning is that this tool does not have ASPNETCore involved at all. It is just a simple console application that runs on an infinite while loop, dequeueing and processing work based on an input parameter that indicates "which type of work it should dequeue/process".

@julealgon The issue here is not just applicable to ASP.NET Core. Anytime an `Activity` is created (or attempted to be created), or a `Measurement` is recorded on Instruments, the runtime takes a lock to figure out the list of listeners to be notified of this thing, leading to contention.

The simple repro is just a console console app:
https://github.com/cijothomas/lock-contention-activity-repro/blob/main/lock-contention-activity-repro/Program.cs

I am still wondering what caused your CPU usage to spike when OTel is enabled.. This issue is unlikely to be the culprit for that - this causes contention and reduce throughput, but I am unsure if it can explain the CPU spike. (It could be some issue in OTel sdks as well.)

> I am still wondering what caused your CPU usage to spike when OTel is enabled.. This issue is unlikely to be the culprit for that - this causes contention and reduce throughput, but I am unsure if it can explain the CPU spike. (It could be some issue in OTel sdks as well.)

We tried basically removing _everything_ but the basic `AddOpenTelemetry` + `UseOtlpProtocol` calls and we _still_ observed crazy CPU usage, so we just "stopped the experiment" there for now. Not much time was invested in a deeper investigation since that work wasn't considered as critical for us at the time.

The only thing that comes to my mind is that maybe the overhead is small, but constant, so that it would go out of control when added 1000 times on the same machine. As I mentioned, this executable is _very_ simple, so any additional overhead on top of what it does becomes substantial, compared to a full-blown API project which is doing a lot more behind the scenes.

That is, of course, just a guess. Maybe the overhead we are seeing is caused not by the instrumentation and listeners, but by the exporter component? I don't know... I even contemplated having a local installation of the OTEL Collector on these 2 servers and have the apps pipe the logs there as an intermediate instead of sending them across to our centralized collector instance, but we did not attempt that test yet. I was a bit discouraged from trying that when I noticed our network graphs did not change much when comparing the before and after (so I assumed the overhead was not with the network back-and-forth and not related to the exporter).

One correction I want to mention after quick looking, is that we don't use any locks when publishing metrics values. The code is here https://source.dot.net/#System.Diagnostics.DiagnosticSource/System/Diagnostics/Metrics/Instrument.common.cs,94. We are currently looking at related issues in metrics when aggregating metrics measurements for out-of-proc EventSource support. I guess this is part causing lock contentions in metrics.

We take a lock though in `ActivitySource` during the notification https://source.dot.net/#System.Diagnostics.DiagnosticSource/System/Diagnostics/ActivitySource.cs,494 as this issue is tracking to fix.

Unless i've done something quite wrong, this should be correct. My methodology was to switch to an immutable copy-on-write approach for modifying the listener collection that uses a CAS to mutate the collection.

It should be noted that this approach will be slightly slower to add/remove listeners because the list of listeners must be copied each time it is mutated. That that performance will degrade with O(N) complexity as the number of listeners grows.

However, that event should be rare compared to creation of Activities which is made much much faster under contention and likely in the uncontented scenario also because the previous approach would acquire/release a lock for each item in the listener collection individually.

Note the above microbenchmark shows a 10x improvement in runtime using the lock-free approach under contention.

Also, there is a *slight* behavioral change. 

- Previously, if a listener was added or removed from the list exactly during the signaling of a single Activity, that change would be observed because the list was being locked/unlocked for each item in the list
- With the proposed change, the Activity thread obtains a local immutable version of the list before it begins signaling listeners.

I doubt anyone will notice this at all and since this is a mutithreaded scenario, there would be no way to reliably reproduce the previous behavior anyway.

- I agree usually creating/adding listeners is done a few times in main scenarios so we can accept some perf degradation there. 
- I didn't see your changes but want to mention, we want to avoid depending on Immutable collections library in System..Diagnostics.DiagnosticSource.dll. because the diagnostic library is low in stack, and we are trying to reduce the dependencies for the sake of AOT scenarios and avoid cyclic dependencies. Considering that, we need to mimic the immutable collection behavior in the fix here.
